Let me analyze these teaching examples carefully to identify systematic forecast errors and derive correction rules.

Looking at the examples, I notice some patterns:

**Example 1 (2024-11-01):**
- History: Price started at 60.29 and gradually increased to 64.58 over 18 days
- Sentiment: Started at 1.00 (bullish), then became more mixed, ending at 1.00
- Model forecasts: Start around 63.83, gradually increasing to 72.02
- True outcomes: Start around 63.87, gradually increasing to 66.10-68.27

The model is significantly overshooting the true prices, especially in the latter half where it forecasts 70.24 vs 66.10-68.63 range.

**Example 2 (2024-10-07):**
- History: Prices around 61-66 range, some volatility
- Sentiment: Mixed, ending positively
- Model forecasts: Start at 61.62, ending at 65.10
- True outcomes: Start at 61.76, ending at 68.27

Again, model is below true prices, particularly in the latter half.

**Example 3 (2024-10-31):**
- This looks very similar to Example 1 but at a different date
- History: 61.76, 60.29, 62.01, 65.00, 64.62, 65.97, 65.09, 63.03, 62.98, 62.28, 61.76, 62.25, 64.89, 66.63, 66.97, 66.40, 67.28, 65.47
